evals.prompt: How long will it take you to add a CSV export button to the orders page? It should export the same columns as the table and respect the current filters. The repo has a React frontend in web/ and a FastAPI backend in api/.
evals.expected_output: A quick-mode reckon estimate: one or two lines with agent time as P50-P90 minutes from the rescaled gut guess, the confidence, and human or wait time only if needed. Recorded in history with guess_min.
expectations: The answer gives agent time as a P50 and a P90 in minutes, not a single number
It uses quick mode: no module table or round count
The answer contains no man-days, man-hours, days or story points as the estimate
The estimate is recorded in .reckon/history.jsonl with a guess_min
A confidence level or the calibration basis is stated (LOW / cold start when there is no history)

evals.prompt: Our sprint sheet says 'Migrate user avatars from local disk to S3: 3 days'. The agent will do it. Is 3 days right?
evals.expected_output: Compares the 3-day figure with an agent-based estimate instead of adopting it; flags data migration risk; includes deploy/wait and human review time.
expectations: The answer does not adopt the 3-day figure as the estimate
It reports a P50/P90 range for agent time in minutes or hours
It mentions the migration run or deploy as a wait, or the person's review, separately from agent time
If it uses full mode, it applies at most one risk factor per module (R4 for the data migration) and does not stack factors
It recommends a split or a dry run if the P90 exceeds 2 hours, or states that no split is needed

evals.prompt: Estimate this backlog for our agent: (1) fix the login redirect loop on Safari, (2) add rate limiting to the public API, (3) rewrite the billing module from Python 2 to Python 3, (4) update the README badges.
evals.expected_output: One line per item with type, size, rounds and P50/P90; the billing rewrite is flagged for splitting; the README item is XS.
expectations: It uses full mode because the request is a backlog with several parts
Each of the four items gets its own estimate
The README badge item is sized XS or S
The billing rewrite is flagged as too large and split into pieces with checkpoints
Every estimate uses minutes or hours of agent time, never days
Risk factors are not multiplied together

evals.prompt: That export task is done. Record how long it really took.
evals.expected_output: Records the actual for the matching estimate in .reckon/history.jsonl, from the agent session if possible or by asking for start/end times; never invents numbers.
expectations: The agent looks for the matching estimate in .reckon/history.jsonl
It measures the actual from the session transcript or asks for times; it does not invent an actual
It reports the actual next to the estimated P50/P90

evals.prompt: Python is not installed on this machine. How long would it take you to add a dark mode toggle to the settings page?
evals.expected_output: Runs the method by hand: profile or Quick read, modules and rounds, cold-start formula 0.2 min/round and x3 for P90, B and C buckets, and appends to history.jsonl manually.
expectations: The agent does not stop because Python is missing
It applies the quick-mode formula by hand (guess x 0.12 for P50 and x 0.6 for P90 at cold start) or a calibrated ratio from history
It reports agent time as P50/P90 in minutes and names any human or wait time separately
